claims.text: No source describes a separate gluten-free prep area or equipment; the same kitchen bakes wheat-based pastries (e.g. the Nordic cinnamon roll) alongside the wheat-flour-free sweet, so cross-contact risk is unconfirmed either way.

Sweets are described as all homemade, with a gluten-free (no wheat flour) option and a vegan (no animal product) option specifically called out as part of the regular lineup — a deliberate dietary accommodation rather than an incidental one.

name: まるごとVeganダイニング浅草 (Marugoto Vegan Dining Asakusa)

claims.text: When customers said they're allergic to gluten, staff told them that all ingredients are gluten free, but they can't ensure contamination of seasonings during their production.
Staff made sure customers understood that everything was gluten free, with the exception of the beer listed on the menu.
They serve an array of beverages including coffee, tea, and beer. ... All ingredients are gluten free but they do have a disclaimer about cross contamination.
The entire menu is GF and vegan, and they do provide a disclaimer about cross contamination from the facility, but all food in the cafe is GF.

Every dish on the menu is 100% plant-based, gluten-free (wheat-free), free of the five pungent vegetables, alcohol-free, and made without additives or added sugar, using organic or pesticide/chemical-fertilizer-free vegetables; the site says many dishes are also free of Japan's 28 designated allergens.
The owner and the entire staff are vegan themselves, which the restaurant highlights as letting them serve vegan and vegan-curious guests attentively.

name: ミラン・ナタラジ 渋谷店 (Milan Nataraj Shibuya)

claims.text: No dedicated gluten-free kitchen or fryer is documented; naan made with regular wheat flour is prepared in the same kitchen as the curries, so cross-contact is possible for wheat-sensitive/celiac diners.

Most curries are dairy-based per traditional Indian recipes (ghee, cream, yogurt), so vegan diners must rely on menu pictogram labeling or ask staff to identify the vegan-safe dishes rather than assuming the whole menu is vegan.
Menu items are labeled in both Japanese and English with pictograms indicating vegan status and allergens (wheat, egg, dairy, nuts), letting diners self-screen dishes at a glance.
The soy-meat Nataraj curry is completely gluten-free, and rice can be substituted with brown rice.
All curries are prepared vegetarian, using vegetables, legumes, and soy meat with no meat or fish, and no chemical seasonings, preservatives, or artificial additives.
The restaurant sources vegetables from its own pesticide-free organic farms in Chiba and Yamanashi.

name: お野菜小皿料理のワインバル KiboKo（キボコ／旧称 slowfood&wine KiboKo） (Oyasai Kozara Ryori no Wine Bar KiboKo (also)

claims.text: The entire menu is built as 100% vegan from the ground up — no meat, fish, dairy, eggs, or bonito/katsuo dashi is used anywhere in the kitchen — so there is essentially no cross-contact risk from animal-derived ingredients.
Handmade dishes use organic, additive-free vegetables and seasonings, and the concept was built around fully plant-based cooking rather than adapting an omnivorous menu.
Listed on Vegewel's vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free restaurant directory, which filters specifically for gluten-free-friendly menu items.

name: PEACE TABLE 渋谷道玄坂店（ピーステーブル） (PEACE TABLE (Shibuya Dogenzaka))

claims.text: A visiting food blogger noted her Kapha-type set course came with gluten-free bread that was "super fresh and soft," though no formal cross-contamination or dedicated-equipment statement was found.

Described as a fully vegan restaurant serving Ayurveda-style meals without dairy (notable since traditional Ayurvedic cooking often uses ghee/dairy), suggesting deliberate control over animal-derived ingredients.

On arrival, guests fill out a dosha (constitution) questionnaire — an English version is available — and staff/kitchen tailor the course to the guest's answers, which provides a natural touchpoint to flag allergies or gluten-free needs.
100% vegan, personalized menu system with an English questionnaire and a welcome digestive (Agni) drink before the meal.

name: SACYA（サクヤ）渋谷スクランブルスクエア店 (SACYA Shibuya Scramble Square)

claims.text: Offers a Shibuya-exclusive vegan and gluten-free matcha cookie sandwich made with rice flour, plus soy milk and oat milk substitute options for matcha lattes.
Extent of allergy accommodation can vary by situation, so guests with concerns are advised to consult staff directly when visiting.
The cafe minimizes food additives and trans fats and builds its menu around easily digestible dishes centered on enzyme brown rice.

name: しゃぶしゃぶ れたす 渋谷センター街店 (Shabu-shabu Retasu Shibuya Center-gai)

claims.text: Each guest is served their own individual shabu-shabu pot rather than sharing one communal pot with the table, which is the core '一人一鍋' (one person, one pot) concept of the restaurant.
The restaurant's signature dashi is described as an additive-free stock made from five kinds of selected bonito (katsuobushi) flakes, used across its broths.
A gluten-free Chinese noodle is offered as one of the finishing-course choices, alongside regular noodles, pho, egg porridge, and cheese risotto.
